recipes.name: Baked Brie
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (17.5 ounce) package frozen puff pastry, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet or line with parchment paper.
Slice Brie cheese wheel in half so you have 2 circles of cheese. Spread preserves on the cut side of one circle of Brie; arrange remaining circle of Brie rind-side up on top.
Wrap the entire wheel of Brie with one sheet of puff pastry; transfer onto the prepared baking sheet seam-side down. Brush puff pastry with egg white.
Bake in the reheated oven until pastry in golden brown, about 30 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Brie
raw_recipe.description: This Brie cheese recipe wraps a round of Brie with apricot preserves in puff pastry; it's baked until the cheese is melted and deliciously gooey inside.

review.reviewBody: This is always a hit!! I use a can of crescent rolls - it's definitely the best way - just roll out the rolls - & follow the rest of the recipe - wrap the dough to cover the cheese & bake. its awesome. (Also, crumble some brown sugar over the egg wash befor baking.)

I read the reviews and also checked another recipe and made the following changes: I froze the brie for about 30 minutes to make slicing easier. I toasted the slivered almonds and put them between the brie halves with the apricot preserves. 
I used a parchment lined baking sheet and bathed the top and sides in an egg wash. I also baked the brie at 425 degrees for 20 minutes. It came out golden brown, the pastry was crispy all over and the cheese was just warm enough to be slightly melted in the center. The flavor was wonderful! 
I think the higher baking temperature is key as the pastry needs to be browned but the cheese needs to be warm but not completely melted. Also, the egg wash is extremely important to achieve browning and letting the brie stand for 5 minutes before cutting.
I'll make this again with cherry preserves and walnuts!

This is great! The way I make it is with pie crust. I use 1 wall of brie, and 12oz preserves. Cut the brie in small cubes, place in pie crust, pour preserves over. Top with pie crust. Bake @ 400 for 25 minutes, serve with crackers.

Cut the Brie using dental floss. Using a long string of floss, wrap it all the way around the outside of the Brie along the cutting line so that the floss creates a loop around the Brie. Pull ends of floss in opposite directions to tighten the loop for a perfect cut.

I normally freeze the Brie for about 30 minutes as it makes cutting the top off the wheel. Then I'll add 4 to 6 tablespoons of Apple Butter and carefully replace the top without pushing it down. Then I'll drape the Puff Pastry over the top and pull the sides tight so im able to flip it over. I Then pull the rest of the Pastry toward the middle as tight as I can without splitting the Pastry already wrapped around the wheel keeping the Apple Butter inside so as the Brie melts it combines with the Apple Butter. Other times I'll scoop out enough Brie to make a pool of sorts for the Apple Butter or use Hot Pepper Jam in the pool. Ill wrap as I normally do and use the leftover Pastry to wrap the Brie i removed making 2 different types of Baked Brie

I made these using 2 tins of Brie (4.4 oz ea) divided into 16 even wedges, and a package of crescent rolls, each piece cut into 2 triangles, for 16 individual appetizers. Party goers said it was their favorite dish of the evening. Once you get the hang of wrapping the cheese and preserves in triangles of pastry, they're easy to put together. I cooked them for 20 minutes at 350 and they came out perfectly.

I have made this recipe with the fruit preserves in the center and it's fantastic. But when I'm in the mood for savory I brush the inside of the dough with melted butter and sprinkle with granulated garlic (instant garlic bread) then put Zesty Red Onion Preserves (Ball's Blue Book) in the center. Talk about wonderful! There is just enough sweetness in the preserves yet it's still considered savory. Serve with garlic crostini. Let it cool down a bit before cutting so it doesn't run out all over your platter.

I am not fond of the rind that is on Brie. So I shaved it off with a potato peeler. WOW what a difference it made to the taste. I could really taste the cheese with out the rind. I also used Polaner apricot spreadable fruit. The combination was spectacular. I made this for Easter and was not sure if my family was going to like it so I made the small wheel. I wished I had bought the large wheel of Brie, it went so fast. I loved this so much that i made the small triangle of Brie about 3 days later for my husband and I. I added the picture of the triangle above. It did ooze out the back a bit but it was still great!.

A hit! Very tasty and easy to make! I chose to use blood orange marmalade (about 5 tablespoons) in between the slices of brie and topped with sliced almonds. I rolled the puff pastry out so that it would be large enough to completely cover the brie. I cut off extra lengths of dough to make a beautiful topper. Brushed with egg white and it was beautiful AND delicious! * I do recommend baking it on a cookie sheet, as some of the filling can leak out if the seams aren't sealed completely. Then transfer to a nice serving dish surrounded by crackers..
Always a hit! I add more preserves than directed. I also add brown sugar and chopped walnuts to the inside. I use filo sheets and brush each layer with butter as I wrap it. Always delicious!

This was a different way to enjoy my favorite brie cheese, and pretty good! I will say, I really enjoyed the apricot preserves- the sweet to salty ratio was wonderful. However, I did have an issue with the cooking & consistency of this dish... Definitely use a pan or dish that has sides to it! Otherwise, if the puff pastry breaks open while cooking (which mine did), you will have an oily mess ALL over your oven! Next time I will use more of the apricot preserves- a generous amount is a good idea if you want to taste it through the puff pastry. I did find the pastry part to be a bit thick and overwhelming. And I also did not brush mine with egg whites, so I will try that next time. I just found the cheese to solidify pretty quickly, again, after baking, so it was a bit difficult & messy to cut into the longer it sat. Maybe making smaller portions would work better? Either way, I really enjoyed the taste & it was very quick and easy to make!

excellent recipe....I used cherry preserves inside and outside with pecans!! I made a small portion in a soufflé cup for me, no pastry, just cheese and preserves. It was delicious and no flour. Huge hit!
Used two wedges rather than a wheel and probably more apricot preserves than were called for. Came out delicious and everyone loved it. Next time I will bake on parchment paper.
It was absolutely delicious. My whole family loved it
The Brie cheese evaporated and the dough was undercooked?? Followed exactly.
